newsitem.title: UK: British bank group stops advising Belgrade on debt.
newsitem.headline: British bank group stops advising Belgrade on debt.

text.p: British banking group National Westminster Plc said on Friday it had withdrawn from its role as adviser to the federal Yugoslav government on negotiations with the Balkan nation's international creditors.
A spokeswoman said the decision followed recent signs that Belgrade had moved away from commitments to economic liberalisation and democratisation.

Crowds of protesters have been thronging the streets of Belgrade for 76 straight days to call on the Serbian government to reverse its refusal to admit that opposition parties won local elections in November in many towns and cities.

"We have indicated to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia that, due to the change in the international climate, we are unable to proceed with our advisory work with them on sovereign debt negotiations," the spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman said National Westminster would continue with technical work on the privatisation of Serbia's PTT telecommunications agency.

She said Belgrade gave commitments to greater economic and political liberalism at the time of the Dayton negotiations which brought peace to Bosnia, but added that "recent actions by the Republic have shown a move away from that commitment".
Yugoslavia is waiting to begin talks with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank on repaying a total of $1.3 billion to the two institutions.
It needs to agree terms on this debt before it can expect new loans to help it rebuild an economy shattered by the Bosnian conflict.
Douglas Hurd, who stepped down as British foreign secretary in July 1995, is deputy chairman of National Westminster's NatWest Capital Markets subsidiary, which was advising Serbia on its debt.
British newspapers have reported that Hurd went to Belgrade last July and had private talks with President Slobodan Milosevic.
